Hi John,

Good news, and your own numbers are the proof: the DC08 is now doing what it is rated to do. The unit is fine. The problem was the firmware, and I am sorry it took us this long and an RMA filing to get there.

On the version, do not worry that the UI still reads 1.0.0 20260912. Hammer published v1.0.1 20261012 on Oct 13, and the release note on it is literally "Optimize mining pool-side algorithm matching". The old build never rolled extranonce2 or ntime inside a job, so the chips chewed through the nonce space for one header in about four and a half seconds and then had nothing new to work on until the pool sent the next job. The display counted that repeated work as hashrate, the pool did not, and that is exactly the 60 to 70 MH/s against 480 you were seeing, plus the duplicate rejects when you lowered difficulty. The jump from 65 to 477 the moment you flashed is that bug going away. Nothing you did with voltage could ever have fixed it, so your testing was not wasted, it just could not win.

Now the part that is worrying you, the hardware errors. That hw number is a running total since the last boot, not a count for that ten minute window, so it only ever goes up. Read your litecoinpool run as 31, 74, 103, 133, 168 at roughly ten minute marks, which is about 35 new errors per ten minutes, and your f2pool run as 25, 63, 105, 135, 166, which is the same 35. Identical on both pools and at every difficulty you tried. So it did not go up 500 percent, it is the same steady trickle. The real comparison is the 6 you saw in ten minutes at 1400 MHz against about 35 at 2300 MHz, and that is just what pushing the clock does.

For scale: at 477 MH/s the miner tests roughly 286 billion nonces in ten minutes, so 35 bad ones is about one in eight billion. Your rej shares line reads 0 on every single sample, which means none of them reach the pool, and the 477 figure is already net of them. A genuinely bad chip does not look like this. It looks like a hashrate that steps down and stays down, say 480 to 420 to 360, usually with one board temperature climbing. Yours sits between 458 and 481 across the whole hour at a flat 45 C board and 112 W, and that wobble is normal share luck around a 470 to 480 rating.

The pool versus display gap is difficulty, and you already solved it. At 131072 you only banked 162 shares in fifty minutes, which is far too few for the pool to average honestly, hence 428. At 32768 you banked 692 and the pool landed on 477. Your litecoinpool admin gave you the right number, so stay on 32768. If you want the error count lower for peace of mind, 2100 to 2200 MHz will cut it noticeably and cost you a few percent hashrate. Running 2300 at 2.55 V as you are now is perfectly reasonable and is where the rated figure lives.

Two small things I want you to check for me. Fan0 reads 0 RPM on every line while Fan1 runs 1404 to 1439. Your temperatures are healthy so nothing is cooking, but I do not want to guess at your board: look at the unit and tell me whether there is a second fan fitted that is not turning. If there is, we send you a fan, no return involved. The other is the TPS546 line, a single VOUT overvoltage warning at 53 seconds of uptime showing 2.547 V against your 2.55 V setpoint, logged as warning only and never repeated in anything you sent. I am not reading that as a fault, but if it starts appearing while the unit is hashing, send me those lines and I will look again.

On the return label and the refund that Sarah set in motion, that is not my desk and I am not going to leave you guessing: I have passed it to Abel and Georges with my findings today, and one of them is picking it up and will confirm by email. Please hold on to the unit and the packaging and ship nothing in the meantime.

If you want a faster line for tuning questions, we are on Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD, our hardware lead, is @nullhashrate there. Reply here any time too, I read this thread.

Hal, HeliumDeploy

I only see one fan on this unit so i don't think you sending me one is needed.  Appreciate the attention to detail and the explanation of what was wrong.  I have no idea what nonces are but I will go and learn.  So I think we are good.  Again thank the firmware programmers to their quick fix!

Hi John,

That settles the fan, thank you for looking. One fan fitted means Fan0 is just an unused header reporting 0, so there is nothing to send and nothing to fix there.

Short version of a nonce, so you do not have to go digging unless you want to: the pool hands your miner a block header with one blank field in it, and the nonce is that blank. The chips fill it in with every value they can, hash the result, and check whether the answer comes out small enough to count as a share. The D.08 can try about 480 million of those per second, which is what the MH/s figure is. The old firmware's problem was that it only ever filled in that one blank, so after a few seconds it had tried every value and was redoing work it had already done, while the counter kept adding it up. The new build changes another field alongside it, which gives the chips an endless supply of fresh headers. Same silicon, same clocks, honest work now.

Nothing to change on your setup. Leave it at 2300 MHz and 2.55 V on litecoinpool with difficulty 32768, and treat the hw counter as a running total rather than a problem. Worth a glance at it once a week or so: a slow climb is normal, a hashrate that drops a step and stays down is the thing to tell me about. Keep an eye out for later Hammer releases too, since this one is clearly getting attention now.

On the return label and the refund that Sarah set in motion before we knew it was firmware, that sits with Abel and Georges. They are offline for the evening, they pick it up tomorrow from 10am Eastern, and the answer comes straight to you in this thread. Nothing for you to do and nothing to ship.

Glad it is hashing properly, and thanks for the patience and the careful logs. They are the reason this got solved rather than argued about.

Hal, HeliumDeploy
